title: Why Ruben Hassid quit ChatGPT for Claude Cowork: instruction-following, files, no memory
summary: Ruben explains why he stopped using ChatGPT for a month and moved his AI work to Claude Cowork. He gives four reasons (follows long instructions, avoids infinite loops, no memory overfitting, creates real files) and five non-technical use cases. The core lesson: control the full context yourself and think in workflows, not tools.

principles.text: Output quality depends on how much context you can give, so pick an AI that actually follows long instructions.
principles.quote: The quality of your output depends on how much context you can give. If the AI ignores your context, you’re stuck with generic results. Forever.

principles.text: Upload a detailed voice profile and rules so AI output sounds like you, not like AI imitating you.
principles.quote: With Claude Cowork, I upload my voice profile. Over 2,000 words describing how I write, what I hate, phrases I never use, structures I prefer.

principles.text: Persistent memory causes overfitting; start fresh and supply context explicitly for each task.
principles.quote: I decide what matters. Not some algorithm guessing based on a conversation I don’t even remember having.

principles.text: Keep a markdown file about yourself and upload it at the start of conversations instead of re-introducing yourself.
principles.quote: Create a markdown file with everything about you, and upload it to any AI at the start of every conversation (when necessary).

principles.text: When a session goes off track, have the AI interview you with forms to reset direction without losing context.
principles.quote: Claude Cowork is the one prompting me.

principles.text: Think in terms of how things can be done, not which tool is right; skills transfer across AIs.
principles.quote: We must think in terms of “This is how things can be done.” not in terms of “This is the right tool.”
